# Kubernetes vault target binding, 2026-10-04

The default tenant vault resolver previously accepted an opaque token and sent it to the native connection's configured server, with no sealed relationship between that credential and its target. This packet checks the actual workspace vault value before credential selection. A full kubeconfig must select one unique context, cluster and user; the selected HTTPS server and exact decoded CA must match the captured native configuration. Unsupported target and authentication overrides refuse with a fixed diagnostic. The existing connection digest captured before vault/audit waits and scoped current-status/configuration recapture before callback remain intact.

The change owns ten paths, recorded in the source freeze. It changes neither vault storage/history, schemas, provider enums, public constructors, direct development sessions nor managed-driver compile guards. It supplies no caller proof, injected privileged broker or manually verified onboarding status. The earlier proposed product onboarding packet remains unedited and stopped. This is its credential-to-target prerequisite, not a public onboarding completion claim.

Existing modeled platform and machine fixtures seal their same synthetic credential with their same target and explicitly synthetic public CA bytes. Their old case titles and assertions remain. The real kind fixture seals its actual bounded guest TokenRequest token with the genuine owning cluster server and CA, preserving namespace/RBAC probes, token lifetime, owning cleanup and title identities. Its invalid-token case carries the deliberately invalid token inside the same valid target binding so the genuine HTTP 401 assertion still tests API credential rejection.

The new parser suite exercises selected-context ambiguity, CA/server mismatches, unsafe endpoint and authentication overrides with synthetic values. The native suite `default Kubernetes vault target binding [postgres; modeled API boundary]` uses independently opened actual PostgreSQL backends, actual tenant-scoped connection repositories and the real encrypted tenant file vault through the default broker. Its only modeled provider boundary is the namespaced ServiceAccount response. It explicitly selects the file vault because the production PostgreSQL vault uses PostgREST; this suite supplies no hosted vault, live TLS/RBAC, browser or grant issuance proof. Its delayed vault/audit cases commit target drift or revocation through the independent backend before releasing the held read.

The native flag is `ZENITH_TEST_KUBERNETES_VAULT_TARGET_REQUIRED=1`, with `ZENITH_TEST_PLATFORM_PG_URL` and canonical registered platform schema 13 required before pool hooks. Missing local PostgreSQL remains a visible skip; a required lane with no PostgreSQL throws. The exact 17 expanded native identities and source hashes are in `CASE-CONTRACT.json`. Canonical mandatory gate registration and CI prerequisite wiring are outside this packet and must precede using these cases as release evidence.

All author-side source imports, compilation, lint, tests, database/service work and commits are unrun. Independent source review, targeted models, actual owning PostgreSQL and a fresh real kind guest run belong to root. The existing final SQL recapture is a read before API callback, not an atomic provider-call fence or cancellation/quiescence proof. Concurrent vault rotation retains the existing read-snapshot behavior; this packet does not redesign credential revocation or store topology. Standard worker packaging and product/browser onboarding acceptance remain open.
